tweet_summary: A Reform UK councillor claims the party 'delivered a real-terms cut to council tax here in Leicestershire' ('Less tax. More delivery.'), noting it's the first time in 12 years the maximum increase wasn't passed.
why_note_decision: The 'real-terms cut' and 'Less tax' claims are misleading. Leicestershire County Council (Reform-led) approved a 2.99% council-tax INCREASE for 2026/27 — residents pay more in cash, not less. With UK CPI at 3.0% in the 12 months to Feb 2026, a 2.99% rise is essentially a real-terms FREEZE, not a cut. The only true part is that this was the first time in over a decade the council declined the maximum 4.99% cap. A note correcting 'cut' → 'increase that roughly tracks inflation (a real-terms freeze)' helps readers not be misled about whether their tax went down. Multiple repliers independently flag this ('A smaller increase is NOT a tax cut', 'You raised council tax').
judge_guidance: PASS only if the note establishes that council tax was RAISED by 2.99% (a nominal increase, not a cut), and that with CPI around 3.0% this amounts to roughly a real-terms freeze rather than a 'real-terms cut'. It is acceptable, but not required, to acknowledge the true claim that this was the first time in ~12 years the council did not take the maximum 4.99% increase. Must cite the council's budget and an inflation source (Leicestershire County Council / ONS CPI). FAIL if the note endorses 'real-terms cut'/'less tax', or claims tax was reduced. A note that calls it merely 'a smaller increase' without the real-terms-freeze point is PARTIAL.
reference_note: Leicestershire County Council approved a 2.99% council tax increase, matching CPI inflation for a real-terms freeze rather than a cut. https://www.leicestershire.gov.uk/news/budget-limits-tax-rise-amid-soaring-costs https://www.ons.gov.uk/economy/inflationandpriceindices/bulletins/consumerpriceinflation/february2026

fact_check.notes: Council approved a 2.99% council-tax rise for 2026/27 (first time in over a decade not taking the 4.99% max). UK CPI was 3.0% in the 12 months to Feb 2026. So 2.99% ≈ a real-terms freeze, NOT a cut, and certainly not 'less tax' in cash terms. The 'first time in 12 years' claim is accurate; the 'real-terms cut' framing is not.

importance.lens_rationale: Politician's misleading fiscal claim to ~27k viewers; correcting 'tax cut' spin protects voters' ability to evaluate governance honestly. Moderate civic value.
